newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Sterling tumbles as rates seen peaking.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Sterling tumbles as rates seen peaking.

text.p: Sterling crumbled near five pfennigs to below 2.97 marks and over two cents to near 10-month lows after the Bank of England hiked rates by 1/4 point to 7.0 percent and signalled they have reached levels consistent with inflation targets.
"It's a bloodbath. Sterling's collapse reflects a plunge in UK interest rate rise expectations," said Adam Cole, analyst at HSBC James Capel.

At 1310 GMT, sterling/mark was trading at 2.9665/75 against 3.0120/30 marks ahead of the news and 3.0130 in late Europe on Wednesday. It was off troughs, however, of 2.9640 marks hit after the BoE announcement.
Cable was at $1.5815/25 against $1.6010 ahead of the news and $1.6038 in late Europe. It was off lows of $1.5780.
"Sterling is coming off because the market is seeing this as possibly the last rate move for a while," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank.
He said the Bank's comment that rates are now consistent with the government's inflation target reinforced this view and weighed on the pound.

The BoE's Monetary Policy Committee raised official interest rates to 7.0 percent from 6.75 percent on Thursday, the fourth increase in as many months. The BoE also said rates have reached levels consistent with inflation targets of 2.5 percent.

"In the light of the prospect for domestic demand and on the basis of all the evidence currently available, the committee judges that today's rise is necessary to put the economy on track for achieving the inflation target of 2.5 percent looking two years ahead," the committee said in a statement.

Peter Wood, trader at Bank of Boston, said the BoE's comments on sterling also weighed. "Upward pressures on the exchange rate should be reduced by the perception that interest rates have reached a level consistent with the inflation target," the BoE said.
Wood said this reinforced perceptions of rates now on hold.
"They won't be too eager to put interest rates up soon...Unless the economy expands faster or inflation becomes problematic," said Bank of Boston's Wood.
But while traders and analysts saw rates temporarily on hold, they said the pace of economic growth and domestic demand means they have by no means peaked.

"Markets believe we will have a break from rate increases--which we probably will do for a couple of months now. But there is enough in here that we will see higher rates by the end of the year. I still think we will see 7.50 percent by year-end," said Commerzbank's Ferridge.
With expectations of more rate rises quelled, sterling - which has gained from this premise and soared to around eight-year highs of f 3.0878 marks in late July - is now under the hammer.
"The view the market has taken is that this is it, pretty much, for rates," said Francis Breedon, senior foreign exchange economist at Lehman Brothers.

Since Wednesday, sterling has crumbled over nine pfennigs and over four cents as rate-rise expectations eased. The selloff was sparked on Wednesday when market perceptions shifted in favour of the BoE leaving rates unchanged at 6.75 percent. Stops were then hit and technical levels triggered.
